en: Theragāthā 2.45 Dukanipāta, Pañcamavagga The Elder Vajjita Thera’s Verse I have crossed over the flood; I am free from all bonds. Having abandoned all attachments, I dwell without clinging. I have reached the further shore; I am a sage (muni) who has attained peace. My mind is well-liberated; I am one who has done what was to be done. I am a bhikkhu who has reached the goal; I am a tamed one, with my burden laid down. I have transcended all states of existence; I am a brahmin who has reached the further shore. I am a true ascetic (śramaṇa), a true brāhmaṇa, and a true monk (bhikṣu). I am a conqueror of all things; I am a victor, having conquered all. I am a stream-enterer, no longer subject to rebirth in the lower realms. With seven more births at most, I shall put an end to suffering. I am a seeker of the path, walking upon the noble way. I am a follower of the Dhamma, established in the Dhamma. I am a forest-dweller, a wearer of rag-robes, and a frequenter of remote lodgings. I am content with little, easily supported, and easy to satisfy. I am one who dwells in solitude, delighting in meditation. I am a speaker of truth, one whose speech is measured. I am one who speaks at the proper time, speaking what is beneficial and true. I am one who speaks gently, speaking words that are pleasing. I am one who speaks with purpose, speaking words that lead to liberation. I am one who does not speak in vain, avoiding idle chatter. I am one who is mindful, possessed of clear comprehension. I am one who is vigilant, ever-attentive to the present moment. I am one who is energetic, possessing unflagging vigor. I am one who is resolute, never turning back from the task. I am one who is wise, endowed with penetrative insight. I am one who sees clearly, possessing the eye of wisdom. I am one who is liberated, released from the bonds of Māra. I am one who is cooled, having attained the bliss of Nibbāna. I am one who is stainless, purified of all defilements. I am one who is bright, shining with the light of Dhamma. I am one who is serene, having attained perfect peace. I am one who is fearless, having overcome all fear. I am one who is confident, possessing the assurance of a Tathāgata. I am one who is self-controlled, having mastered my own mind. I am one who is tamed, like a well-broken thoroughbred horse. I am one who is subdued, having brought my senses under control. I am one who is tranquil, having attained inner stillness. I am one who is composed, established in equanimity.

I am one who is emancipated, having crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra. I am one who is enlightened, having realized the Four Noble Truths. I am one who is awakened, having dispelled the darkness of ignorance. I am one who is fully awakened, the peerless Buddha. I am one who has attained the goal, having reached the end of suffering. I am one who has lived the holy life, having fulfilled the training. I am one who has laid down the burden, having cast off the heavy load. I am one who has accomplished the task, having achieved the purpose of my life. I am one who has severed the fetters, having destroyed the bonds of craving. I am one who has no more birth, having attained final Nibbāna. I am one who has reached the ultimate, having attained the supreme security. I am one who has attained the unconditioned, having entered the deathless state. I am one who has attained the island, having found refuge in the Dhamma. I am one who has attained the shelter, having taken refuge in the Triple Gem. I am one who has attained the light, having dispelled the darkness of delusion. I am one who has attained the radiance, shining with the light of wisdom. I am one who has attained the glory, having become a field of merit for the world. I am one who has attained the victory, having conquered the army of Māra. I am one who has attained the sovereignty, having become a master of myself. I am one who has attained the mastery, having gained power over my own mind. I am one who has attained the perfection, having fulfilled all virtues. I am one who has attained the excellence, having surpassed all beings. I am one who has attained the supremacy, having become the highest among men. I am one who has attained the preeminence, having become the foremost of those who have crossed over. I am one who has attained the leadership, having become the guide of the world. I am one who has attained the guidance, having shown the path to liberation. I am one who has attained the direction, having pointed out the way to Nibbāna. I am one who has attained the instruction, having taught the Dhamma. I am one who has attained the teaching, having established the Dispensation. I am one who has attained the proclamation, having declared the truth. I am one who has attained the revelation, having unveiled the hidden meaning. I am one who has attained the manifestation, having made the Dhamma known. I am one who has attained the disclosure, having explained the profound truths. I am one who has attained the exposition, having analyzed the teachings. I am one who has attained the elucidation, having clarified the subtle points. I am one who has attained the illumination, having shone the light of Dhamma. I am one who has attained the enlightenment, having awakened to the truth. I am one who has attained the awakening, having realized the nature of reality. I am one who has attained the full awakening, having become a Buddha. I am one who has attained the complete awakening, having reached the pinnacle of knowledge. I am one who has attained the ultimate awakening, having transcended all worldly states. I am one who has attained the final awakening, having reached the end of the journey. I am one who has attained the absolute awakening, having realized the unconditioned. I am one who has attained the unsurpassed awakening, having become the peerless teacher. I am one who has attained the incomparable awakening, having no equal in the world. I am one who has attained the matchless awakening, having no rival in the three worlds. I am one who has attained the unequaled awakening, having no counterpart in the universe. I am one who has attained the peerless awakening, having no likeness among gods or men. I am one who has attained the incomparable awakening, having no superior in the realm of existence. I am one who has attained the unequalled awakening, having no equal in the entire cosmos. I am one who has attained the unparallelled awakening, having no counterpart in the great earth. I am one who has attained the unmatched awakening, having no rival in the vast ocean. I am one who has attained the unrivaled awakening, having no opponent in the great mountain range. I am one who has attained the unrivalled awakening, having no adversary in the boundless sky. I am one who has attained the unopposed awakening, having no obstacle in the infinite space. I am one who has attained the unobstructed awakening, having no hindrance in the eternal Dhamma. I am one who has attained the unhindered awakening, having no barrier in the ultimate truth. I am one who has attained the unimpeded awakening, having no blockage in the pure mind. I am one who has attained the unconfined awakening, having no limit in the vast expanse. I am one who has attained the unlimited awakening, having no boundary in the infinite wisdom. I am one who has attained the measureless awakening, having no scale in the immeasurable virtue. I am one who has attained the boundless awakening, having no end in the endless compassion. I am one who has attained the infinite awakening, having no limit in the limitless love. I am one who has attained the eternal awakening, having no change in the constant Dhamma. I am one who has attained the timeless awakening, having no beginning or end in the cycle of birth and death. I am one who has attained the deathless awakening, having reached the state beyond all decay. I am one who has attained the immortal awakening, having entered the city of Nibbāna. I am one who has attained the undying awakening, having extinguished the fires of greed, hatred, and delusion. I am one who has attained the unaging awakening, having transcended the process of becoming. I am one who has attained the sorrowless awakening, having put an end to all suffering. I am one who has attained the stainless awakening, having washed away all impurities. I am one who has attained the pure awakening, having become stainless and radiant. I am
The Verses of the Elder Visākhapañcālaputta:
“One should not lift up others, nor should one cast them down;
one should not push back those who have reached the further shore, nor should one shake them.”
One should not speak disparagingly of others in assemblies;
being undisturbed, moderate in speech, and observant of vows,
one should be a seer of the most subtle and refined meaning.
For one who is skilled in wisdom, humble in conduct,
and who has cultivated the virtues of the elders,
nibbāna is indeed not difficult to attain.
